ledger.x: 853 BC (first attestation): Hamath stands on the Orontes.

c. 796 BC: Luhuti joins Hamath. 'Luhuti was incorporated into Hamath around 796 BC. It formed the northern province of the kingdom.' Zakkur is 'king of Hamath and Luhuti'. Where Luhuti lay is not on the page; the Idlib governorate is the reading from Zakkur's fortress at Tell Afis.
738 BC: Hamath becomes an Assyrian tributary.

c. 720 BC: Yahu-Bihdi's revolt ends the tributary state. 'Yahu-Bihdi of Hama in Syria assembled a coalition of minor states' (Arpad, Damascus, Sumur, Samaria) 'shortly after' Sargon's failure in Babylonia in 720; 'Sargon engaged Yahu-Bihdi and his coalition at Qarqar on the Orontes'.

c. 720 BC: Sargon II annexes Hamath. 'Hama and the other insurgent cities were annexed again'; the Hamath page: 'Sargon II razed the city c. 720 BC', 'removed its king to be flayed alive in Assyria' and recolonized it with 6,300 Assyrians.
c. 720 BC: the kingdom of Hamath ends under Sargon II. The Aramean displaced from Hamath formed part of the community 'in Egypt starting in 700 BCE'.

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar
wars.outcome: Assyrian claim of victory; 'Shalmaneser's opponents held on to their thrones after this battle'.

wars.name: Siege of Hazrak (Zakkur against the Aramean coalition)
wars.outcome: 'Zakkur survived the siege' at Tell Afis; the coalition was incited by Ben-Hadad III and led by the king of Bit Agusi.

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III's campaigns against Hamath
wars.outcome: Towns of Hamath taken in 743; Hamath again conquered in 738; the province of Hatarikka created.

wars.name: Revolt of Yahu-Bihdi against Sargon II
wars.outcome: Sargon II defeats Yahu-Bihdi at Qarqar on the Orontes, razes Hamath and annexes it as a province.

certainty.note: No Hamathite boundary is given; the Arpad border was a dispute settled by Assyria c.
